common.tagline: Your turn, guaranteed. No fire needed.
common.simulatedLong: Every farmer, field and breakdown here is simulated. Village names and locations are real (OpenStreetMap).
common.errorBody: The planning service did not answer. Your promises are safe; try again in a moment.
common.unreviewedLanguage: Translation not yet reviewed by a speaker

landing.heroTitle: Every farmer gets a date for the machine. Nobody has to burn while waiting.
landing.heroBody: Vaari plans a Custom Hiring Centre's Super Seeders across a village cluster and gives each farmer a promised sowing date. When a machine breaks, it re-plans without silently breaking a promise.
landing.tryNote: One click, no sign-up. Demo accounts on a simulated season.
landing.farmerRoleBody: Sees one date in large type: firm for the next two days, a window further out that narrows to a firm date. If it moves, the reason is right there.
landing.operatorRoleBody: Opens tomorrow's plan: each machine's stops in order, who is at burn risk, one button to approve. Marks a machine as broken and watches the plan re-form.
landing.how1Body: Constraint programming (OR-Tools CP-SAT) assigns fields to machines and days. Every promise is a hard constraint.
landing.how2Body: Tomorrow's route for each machine waits for one approval. Windows become firm dates only then.
landing.how3Body: Ask "why this date?" and Vaari re-runs the solver with your field one day earlier. What blocks it becomes the reason.
landing.fact1: Uncertainty over when a machine will arrive is a main reason farmers burn stubble.
landing.fact2: Each week of sowing delay past the optimum costs about 150 kg of wheat per acre.
landing.honestyTitle: What is real and what is simulated
landing.honestyBody: The farmers, fields, machines and breakdowns in this demo are simulated. Village names and locations come from OpenStreetMap. The sowing optimum (first fortnight of November) is from PAU. Harvest timing will be calibrated from NASA FIRMS fire detections; satellites show heat, not intent.
landing.fireMapPending: Not connected yet. It will show NASA FIRMS detections over Sangrur from the last 24 hours, as a lower bound: satellites pass once or twice a day and miss some fires.

proof.title: Does a promised date actually help?
proof.body: Vaari will be compared with two ways CHCs work today, on the same simulated seasons: a phone queue (first come, first served) and nearest village next.
proof.notRunBody: The results table stays empty until the 200-season simulation has actually run. We do not estimate or fill in numbers.
proof.metric1: Fields sown after the farmer's last waiting day
proof.metric2: Acres sown after the optimum, and wheat lost (150 kg per acre per week, PAU)
proof.metric5: Acres per machine and operator income
proof.metric6: Worst delay compared with the phone queue
proof.spreadNote: Every figure is reported as a median with the 10th to 90th percentile spread, never a single run.
proof.assumption1: Road distance is straight-line distance times 1.3, at 20 km/h (assumed).
proof.assumption2: Super Seeder speed starts anywhere from 5.3 (CEEW) to 12 (district office) acres a day and is learned from logs.
proof.assumption3: Field sizes, waiting limits (3–10 days) and breakdown chance are swept, not fixed.
